input: # quotes.tsv - the three quote characters: as CSS text, and stray.
# The cssToken matcher owns every quote CSS has. Its scans skip a quoted
# run, "..." or '...', inside a selector, a value or a prelude, and the AST
# keeps it verbatim, quotes and escapes included. A backtick is not a CSS
# quote, so the matcher reads it as an ordinary character. The engine's own
# string matcher is OFF (ts/src/css.ts: `string: { chars: '' }`), so a
# quote the matcher declines, at a statement or property position or after
# the last rule, reaches the grammar as an unexpected character:
# Every row in the first two groups used to fail in Go. go/css.go said
# `StringOptions{Chars: ""}`, and in the Go engine an empty Chars means
# UNSET, not none, so the default quotes stayed on: unterminated_string, or
# unprintable where a newline follows the quote, or invalid_unicode /
# invalid_ascii where a \u or \x escape does. It says `Lex: false` now,
# the engine's way to turn string matching off.
# reworkcss/css reads an unmatched quote as an ordinary character, so it
# accepts some inputs these rows reject (a"b\nc{d:e} is a rule there, and
# a{b:"c} has the value "c). The rows pin the canonical port, not reworkcss.
# Stray quotes: declined by the cssToken matcher, unexpected in the grammar.
# A stray quote followed by an escape. The engine's string matcher reads \u
# and \x escapes; with it on, the old Go raised invalid_unicode or
# invalid_ascii here. With it off the quote is unexpected, as in TS.
# Balanced quotes: skipped by the matcher's scans and kept verbatim.
# Backticks: text wherever the matcher reads text, unexpected where it
# declines one. A " or ' after a backtick is not protected by it.
# An unterminated quote inside a selector, value or block: the matcher's
# scans skip a quoted run to its closing quote or the end of the source, so
# nothing after the quote is read as structure.
